steps.label: Parthenocarpic fruit
lines: A fruit that develops from the ovary WITHOUT
steps.why: The one scoring phrase is 'without fertilisation' - the ovary ripens into a fruit though no ovule was fertilised, so no seeds form.
common_mistakes: Confusing parthenocarpy (fruit without fertilisation) with parthenogenesis (embryo from an unfertilised gamete).
steps.memory_tip: Partheno - without fertilisation; carpy - fruit. Banana is the everyday example.
steps.margin_note: Definition + banana; the book's phrase 'unfertilized ripened ovary' is also accepted.

steps.label: Usefulness

lines.text: Such fruits are seedless, so they are

lines: commercially useful in the fruit juice and
steps.why: No fertilisation means no seeds; seedless pulp is what the juice industry wants - the use follows from the definition.
common_mistakes: Writing that the fruits are more nutritious. The commercial value is the absence of seeds, not nutrition.
steps.memory_tip: No fertilisation, no seeds, easy juice.
steps.margin_note: Seedless + juice industry - two phrases, one line.
